children: slides 3.5% in Wednesday's trading to its lowest since September 2022 as UBS downgraded the California utility company to Neutral from Buy with a $14 price target, cut from $19, citing a growing risk of inaction on wildfire liability reform this year and the company’s decision to rescind its long-term earnings growth rate guidance alongside its

California Governor Newsom in recent days has discussed calling a special session of the state legislature on artificial intelligence without mentioning wildfire issues, while gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra has been more vocal about addressing wildfire reform, which delays the potential catalyst for PG&E
shares, UBS analyst Gregg Orrill said.
Orrill lowered his long-term EPS growth rate forecast for PG&E

to 8.5% from 9% as he compounded the company's $2B capital expenditure deferral in 2027-30 and noted that tax loss selling pressure and interest rate risk make the stock incrementally less attractive.

The analyst also cut his FY 2028 EPS estimate to $1.90 from $1.95 and his five-year capital spending outlook by $6B to $65.5B, after the company recently deferred $2B in 2027 capex from the growth category.

title: PG&E drops to nearly four-year low after UBS downgrades as wildfire reform catalyst fades
